newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil seeks to raise limit on debt issues.
newsitem.headline: Brazil seeks to raise limit on debt issues.

text.p: Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso has asked lawmakers to raise the limit on the amount of debt the government can issue in global markets to $10 billion from $5.0 billion, the presidency said Monday.

"We have sent the Senate a message from the president requesting the increase," said a spokeswoman at the presidency. Senators will then decide whether or not to raise Brazil's exisiting ceiling, which was set in 1995, she said.
The federal government has issued a total of about $3.5 billion in foreign debt since 1995 and has plans to price a $300 million Italian lire deal sometime in May.

The Senate was expected to approve the $5.0 billion increase, which is quite small by regional standards. By comparison, the governments of Argentina and Mexico plan to issue $8.5 billion and $4.4 billion, respectively, in 1997 alone.
